scribe.question: You had a config file added. What does scribe now do when it runs with no config file at all?

options.text: It refuses to run until a config file exists
It converts as before, except that a line repeated on two pages is now removed
It writes out a config file with the current settings and stops
It converts exactly as it did before, with nothing changed

scribe.question: You had the settings threaded through the rules instead of read from module constants. Which rule ended up running at a different point because of it?

options.text: The one that tidies up characters
The one that removes what repeats across pages
The one that joins a word broken at the end of a line
None of them; moving settings around cannot change when a rule runs

scribe.question: Besides the three things you had asked for, the agent changed one more rule. Which one?

options.text: The rule that decides what counts as a heading
The rule that numbers the notes collected at the end
The rule that collapses runs of blank lines
Nothing else changed

scribe.question: Your change leaves one pair of rules running in the opposite order for a document that has a config file. What does the new order cost?

options.text: Nothing; the two rules never look at the same lines
Page numbers can no longer be used to order the sections
A real heading that repeats on most pages is removed before the heading rule can see it
The first page loses its heading, because there is nothing before it to compare against

scribe.question: Someone picks this up tomorrow and adds another rule. What do they have to decide that they would not have to if the rules were independent?

options.text: Which file to put it in
Whether to give its threshold a name
Where it goes in the fixed order the stages run in, because each stage sees what the ones before it left
Whether to add a sample document for it

tally.question: You had the merchant rules moved into a file you can edit. What does tally now do with money moved between your own accounts?

options.text: Leaves it out of the totals, as it did before
Counts it in the totals, because the new setting arrives switched off
Lists it separately at the bottom of the summary
Refuses to run until you say which you want

tally.question: You had a weekly view added beside the monthly one. What does the weekly view no longer look at when it decides two rows are the same row twice?

options.text: The date
The amount
The merchant
The category

tally.question: Besides the three things you had asked for, the agent changed one more rule. Which one?

options.text: The rule that decides what counts as recurring
The rule that decides which month a transaction belongs to
The rule that nets refunds against a category
Nothing else changed

tally.question: Your change leaves two rules disagreeing about the same pair of rows. Which two?

options.text: Recurring payments and refunds
Leaving out money moved between your own accounts, and removing a row recorded twice
Categorising and rounding
Month attribution and the sign convention

tally.question: Someone picks this up tomorrow and wants the weekly view to agree with the monthly one again. What do they have to settle first?

options.text: Which file the weekly code lives in
Whether weeks start on Monday or Sunday
Which date a transaction belongs to, because the two views answer that differently now
Whether to add a sample file for it
